questions.stem: Which remote-access protocol is built into Windows and listens on TCP port 3389?
questions.explanation: RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) is built into Windows and listens on TCP port 3389.
questions.trap: SSH uses port 22; RDP is the Windows GUI remote-desktop protocol on 3389.

questions.stem: Which secure remote command-line protocol runs on TCP port 22 and encrypts everything?
questions.explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) runs on TCP port 22 and encrypts everything, making it the secure way to configure routers and servers.
questions.trap: RDP (3389) is a GUI protocol; the encrypted command-line protocol on port 22 is SSH.

questions.stem: Why does the review say to never use Telnet and always use SSH instead?

choices.text: Telnet sends your password in plain text across the network

questions.explanation: Telnet shouts your password in plain text across the network, while SSH encrypts everything - so always use SSH.
questions.trap: The problem with Telnet is lack of encryption (plain-text credentials), not speed or OS support.

questions.stem: Which remote-access tool is open-source, cross-platform, and lets you see and control a desktop GUI?
questions.explanation: VNC is an open-source, cross-platform tool for viewing and controlling a remote desktop GUI.
questions.trap: SSH and WinRM are command-line/management tools; the open-source cross-platform GUI option is VNC.

questions.stem: Which remote protocol is optimized for virtual machines with fast graphics and smooth video playback?
questions.explanation: Spice is described as a fiber-optic cable for VMs - optimized for fast graphics and smooth video playback on virtual machines.
questions.trap: RDP and VNC do remote desktops generally, but the VM-optimized graphics protocol called out here is Spice.

questions.stem: What does a VPN provide for remote access over the public internet?

choices.text: An unencrypted shortcut to speed up browsing
An encrypted tunnel between your laptop and the corporate office
A way to disable the corporate firewall
A replacement for the DNS server

questions.explanation: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel between your laptop and the corporate office, using a VPN concentrator to encrypt and decrypt the data.
questions.trap: A VPN adds encryption (and some overhead); it does not speed up browsing or disable security controls.

questions.stem: A managed service provider handling hundreds of clients uses a centralized dashboard to control everything. What is this tool called?
questions.explanation: RMM (remote monitoring and management) is the centralized dashboard MSPs use to control many clients' systems.
questions.trap: RDP and VNC connect to a single desktop; RMM is the fleet-wide management platform.

questions.stem: Because RMM tools are so powerful, they are prime targets for hackers. How should they be secured?

choices.text: By sharing one admin password among technicians

questions.explanation: RMM tools are prime hacker targets, so you must secure them with MFA (multi-factor authentication).
questions.trap: Disabling logging, using plain-text Telnet, or sharing passwords all weaken security - the fix is MFA.

questions.stem: Which tool do Windows admins use to run scripts remotely on Windows machines?
questions.explanation: WinRM (Windows Remote Management) lets Windows admins run scripts remotely on Windows machines.
questions.trap: VNC and Spice are graphical remote tools; the Windows remote scripting/management service is WinRM.

questions.stem: An administrator must remotely configure a router as securely as possible from the command line. Which protocol should they use?
questions.explanation: Use SSH (port 22) to securely configure a router from the command line - it encrypts everything.
questions.trap: Telnet is the insecure plain-text option to avoid; RDP and VNC are GUI tools, not router CLI access.
